comments.author: soniya-malviy
comments.body_normalized:
@stefansimik  and @RRosio

I’d like to work on this issue and would appreciate being assigned to it.

I’ve been able to reproduce the bug consistently on JupyterLab 4.x and main. After inspecting the DOM with Chrome DevTools, I believe this is not a CSS or theme issue, but a logic issue in the Markdown → HTML rendering pipeline.

**What’s going wrong**

When a fenced code block contains only a single identifier (e.g. x, var), the rendered output becomes an empty <code> block.
When the content is a number (e.g. 1), it renders correctly.
Removing the language specifier or disabling highlighting also makes the identifier appear.

**Analysis so far**

In the Markdown rendering path, when no ANSI sequences are present, a fast-path sanitization is used.
In this case, that path can result in no text node or span being emitted for single-token identifiers.
The <code class="language-python"> element exists, but it is empty, which matches what we see in DevTools.

**Evidence**

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2a1990f-cc87-44b1-a571-3ad4bb9a7384)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e80e7d29-4188-4610-b3a2-29aec8a72fbf)

I’ve attached screenshots showing:
A numeric literal rendering correctly with a <span> inside the code block

```
✅
```python
1
```
```

A single identifier resulting in an empty <code> element

❌
```python
y
```

The corresponding DOM difference in DevTools


Status
I understand where the issue is happening, but my current local attempt is not fully working yet. I’m continuing to iterate on a fix and want to make sure it aligns with the intended design.
If anyone has suggestions on the preferred approach or pointers to similar past fixes in this area, I’d really appreciate the guidance.
If this direction looks reasonable, I’m happy to proceed and open a PR once the fix is solid.
Thanks!

comments.body_normalized:
@krassowski and @RRosio

I've submitted this PR to fix the single-character code block rendering issue. The solution adds minimal defensive handling in renderMarkdown to ensure empty code blocks get proper content.

With your permission, I'd be happy to add comprehensive test cases covering:
Single-character variables (x, y, z)
Single-digit numbers (verifying they still work)
Edge cases and different programming languages
Security validation for proper HTML escaping

Please let me know if you'd like me to proceed with test implementation or if you have any specific testing requirements for this fix.
